nodes.name: ZIF-67 growth
nodes.procedure: The Cu(OH)₂ nanorod arrays prepared by wet-chemical oxidation exhibited cation exchange effects under the influence of Co²⁺. Owing to the coordination between 2-methylimidazole (2-Melm) anchored on the nanorod arrays surface and Co²⁺, ZIF-67 grew uniformly on the Cu(OH)₂ nanorod arrays.

nodes.description: Controlled-potential NRA measurement at -0.3 V vs RHE (standard condition)
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic NRA performance was evaluated in an H-type electrolytic cell employing a standard three-electrode configuration... At -0.3 V vs. RHE, the catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) for NH₃ of 96.35%, with a maximum NH₃ production rate of 1.59 mmol h⁻¹ cm⁻². The calculated Cdl values for CoP/Cu₃P-CF is 73.48 mF cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM reveals surface potential oscillation unique to CoP/Cu₃P heterojunction, confirming broad adsorption energy distribution and synergistic catalytic sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Kelvin probe force microscopy and in situ characterization confirmed a broad adsorption energy distribution conducive to multi-site synergistic catalysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows heterointerfaces with lattice spacing of 0.289 nm for CoP (011) plane and 0.35 nm for Cu₃P (223) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured lattice spacing of 0.289 nm in region I corresponds to the (011) plane of CoP, while the 0.35 nm spacing in region II is assigned to the (223) plane of Cu₃P.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping reveal homogeneous distribution of Cu, Co, P, C, and N elements throughout the CoP/Cu₃P-CF nanorod arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping analysis reveal distinct elemental distribution characteristics.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows diffraction peaks matching CoP (PDF#71-2261), Cu₃P (PDF#29-0497), and Cu (PDF#04-0836) with weak CoP peaks due to lower content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Figure S8), the diffraction peaks of CoP/Cu₃P-CF and Cu₃P-CF match well with the standard references for CoP (PDF#71-2261), Cu₃P (PDF#29-0497), and Cu (PDF#04-0836).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Cu 2p shows peaks at 932.05-932.59 eV (Cu⁰/Cu⁺) shifted to higher binding energy in CoP/Cu₃P vs Cu₃P indicating Cu electron loss; Co 2p at 780.24 eV shifted lower vs CoP (779.63 eV) indicating Co electron gain; P 2p shifts confirm electron bridging role.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Cu 2p high-resolution spectrum (Figure 2a), the binding energy peaks located between 932.05 eV and 932.59 eV in CoP/Cu₃P and Cu₃P are associated to Cu⁰/Cu⁺, respectively... The Co characteristic peak in CoP/Cu₃P (780.24 eV) shifts toward lower binding energy compared to that in CoP (779.63 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES shows absorption edge between Cu foil and CuO indicating Cuδ⁺; Co K-edge between Co foil and CoO indicating Co valence between 0 and +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cu K-edge XANES profiles show that the absorption edge of Cu in CoP/Cu₃P is located between Co foil and CuO, elucidating the formation of Cuδ⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge EXAFS shows Cu-P bond peak at 1-3 Å; Co K-edge shows Co-P coordination at 1.72 Å; WT-EXAFS confirms Cu-P and Co-P structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a dominant peak from 1 to 3 Å was observed in the Cu K-edge EXAFS profile of CoP/Cu₃P, implying the presence of Cu-P bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region yields Cdl=73.48 mF cm⁻² for CoP/Cu₃P-CF (> CoP-CF: 17.34 mF cm⁻², Cu₃P-CF: 36.37 mF cm⁻²), indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Cdl values for CoP/Cu₃P-CF is 73.48 mF cm⁻², which is larger than those of CoP-CF (17.34 mF cm⁻²) and Cu₃P-CF (36.37 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows CoP/Cu₃P-CF has lowest charge transfer resistance Rct among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CoP/Cu₃P-CF shows the lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct) among the as-prepared samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows absorption bands at 1460 cm⁻¹ (NHx), 1668 cm⁻¹ (*H₂O), 1620 cm⁻¹ (*NO), 1123 cm⁻¹ (*NOH); higher *NO₂ intensity indicates faster *NO₃→*NO₂ conversion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: five obvious absorption bands can be observed... The peaks observed at 1668, 1620, and 1123 cm⁻¹ were ascribed to the *H₂O, *NO, and *NOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: *NO₃ peak at 1047 cm⁻¹ disappears after -0.35 V vs RHE for CoP/Cu₃P (faster than Cu₃P/CoP); higher *NH₃ peak intensity confirms enhanced activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the characteristic *NO₃ peak intensity at 1047 cm⁻¹ for CoP/Cu₃P rapidly diminishes and completely disappears after -0.35 V vs. RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ DEMS shows strongest NH₃ signal (~134× stronger than *NO) and weakest H₂ signal for CoP/Cu₃P vs single components, confirming high NH₃ selectivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the signal of NH₃ of CoP/Cu₃P is the most obvious, being approximately 134 times stronger than that of *NO and other nitrogen-containing species.
